title: Windows Phone 7 and the Metro interface
lede: The 2010 phone operating system that introduced Metro by name, with a Start screen of flat colored live tiles.
summary: Start screen of flat live tiles in one accent color on black or white, large type, and panoramic hubs. Microsoft, 2010.

evidence.note: Wikipedia articles on Windows Phone 7 and on Metro read on 2026-09-28. The only interface image found was a 481 × 207 non-free crop of the Music + Video hub on English Wikipedia, too small to count as observed.

styles.note: The first product in which Microsoft named and shipped Metro; the origin of the tile grammar of this record.

context: Windows Phone 7 was released worldwide on 21 October 2010 and in the United States on 8 November 2010. “It was designed with the distinct flat-style Metro interface.” ([Wikipedia: Windows Phone 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Phone_7)).

The home screen, “Start screen”, is made up of live tiles that link to apps, contacts, and other items and update in real time. The default theme is dark; users can choose a light theme and an accent color, and tiles appear in that color.

Metro “was formally introduced as Metro during the unveiling of Windows Phone 7 in 2010”. Its designers cite transport signage as inspiration, and it uses Segoe fonts, including a Segoe WP family made for the phone ([Wikipedia: Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_(design_language))).

The Industrial Designers Society of America gave Windows Phone 7 a Gold Interactive award, a People’s Choice award, and Best in Show at IDEA 2011 ([Wikipedia: Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_(design_language))).
interpretation: The single-accent tile grid is the most compact statement of the style: content and type instead of chrome, and color as the only surface treatment.
